subject: BYO key short-window request — clarify which audit log IDs we must surface
messages:
From: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@acmecorp.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: BYOK short retention window — what audit IDs do you need?

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two quick things from our security team: they want to enable BYOK for our PII-sensitive flows but only for a 7-day short window (to meet a legal hold exemption). As part of that ask they need to see what audit/log IDs Redwood will surface so they can map them to our SIEM.

I've attached our initial BYO requirements doc and a simple syslog field matrix. Can you confirm:
- the names/IDs of the audit events that will indicate key creation, key usage (encrypt/decrypt), key rotation, and key deletion 
- whether you emit a persistent keystore ID or ephemeral key fingerprint for each request
- whether request-level metadata (requesting service, route, model, token counts) is included in the same log entry or only in separate traces

Our compliance deadline for a pilot is next Friday (2026-12-24). If this requires an exception (short window BYOK) in your product, what minimal evidence can you provide immediately so our security can sign off for the pilot?

Cc'ing Priyom and Marissa to loop in product and ops.

Appreciate a quick alignment — Sara

--
Sara Hunt
Senior InfoSec Manager, ACME Corp
security@acmecorp.com
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: BYOK short retention window — what audit IDs do you need?

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments, useful to see ACME's mapping. High level from ops/product: we can support a 7-day BYOK pilot, but there are two vectors to clarify before we hand this to engineering:

1) Audit surface: Redwood emits both a persistent keystore_id (stable for the tenant) and per-request key_fingerprint when ephemeral keys are used. The events we already log are (internal event IDs in parentheses):
   - key.created (ev_key_create)
   - key.used (ev_key_encrypt/decrypt)
   - key.rotated (ev_key_rotate)
   - key.deleted (ev_key_delete)
   - request.accepted (ev_req_accept) — ties request -> keystore usage

2) Metadata: request-level metadata (route, model, tenant_id, token_count) is included by default in the request.accepted event; we also emit a separate trace that links request IDs to hardware node and batch id when requested for forensics.

However — the short-window BYOK scenario has two product constraints: we normally persist minimal key material references in audit logs for 90 days. For a 7-day window we need an exception path that guarantees logs required by your SIEM are available for that 7-day period and then rotated/removed per your retention. That will require engineering work to:
   - add a short-window retention toggle per tenant in the audit pipeline
   - document exactly which fields are retained and how we redact keys/fingerprints after expiry

Action items proposal:
- Product (Marissa) to approve a scoped field set for the pilot (minimal set to satisfy ACME).
- Infra/Platform (Karthik/Priyom) to confirm whether we can fast-track a tenant-level toggle and estimate effort.
- Security (Markus) to provide a temporary evidence bundle (log samples) for ACME to review.

Can Product + Infra weigh in on the minimal field set and a rough ETA? If we can agree this morning, I can push a small evidence package by EOD for ACME's security review.

Thanks,
Markus

--
Markus Klein

Subject: Re: BYOK short retention window — what audit IDs do you need?

Markus / team — quick product take: for a pilot we should surface a minimal, well-documented field set rather than every internal event. My recommended minimal fields for ACME to map into their SIEM: 

- timestamp (ISO8601)
- tenant_id
- keystore_id (persistent tenant-level ID)
- key_fingerprint (per-request when ephemeral)
- event_type (key.created/key.used/key.rotated/key.deleted/request.accepted)
- request_id
- model_id / route
- action (encrypt/decrypt)
- token_count

Notes: 
- We should redact any secret material (never include raw key bytes).
- For the 7-day window, product will accept a scoped exception that keeps these fields in the audit sink for 7 days; afterwards we either null key_fingerprint or remove entries depending on compliance preference.

If Infra can confirm a tentative ETA (preferably <10 working days) for the tenant toggle and controlled retention pipeline, I'll draft the minimal-runbook and hand to Markus to include in the evidence bundle.

Marissa

Subject: Re: BYOK short retention window — what audit IDs do you need?

Thanks all — infra check-in from my side. Technical clarifications and constraints: 

- We already emit the event IDs Markus listed into our audit Kafka topic and they are picked up by the audit pipeline that writes to the long-term ELK cluster. We can add a tenant-level retention override but it will touch three layers: producer (small flag on request), pipeline (transform and TTL), and sink (policy to delete/expire).
- Quick ETA: scoped pilot toggle + pipeline transform (no UI) = ~6 business days if we prioritize (small team, will require an on-call mitigation plan).
- On deletion semantics: we can either null the key_fingerprint after TTL (safer for forensics because event footprint remains) or remove the full event from the sink (harder to guarantee across downstream backups). Recommend nulling fingerprint and adding a retention_delete marker to the event.
- For the evidence bundle: we can provide a sanitized log sample (with token_count and request_id) and a short runbook for how retention will behave during/after the 7-day window. I will coordinate with Priyom on operational playbook.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Marissa: finalize minimal field set (use your list above)
2) Priyom/Karthik: prepare sanitized sample logs + runbook (ETA Wednesday next week 2026-12-23)
3) Markus: assemble evidence package and send to ACME security for signoff

I'll open a quick Jira ticket and tag you all.

Karthik
